output: {"answers":{"d05":"检测出阳性，你真正想知道的是「阳性的人里有多少真患病」。设患病率1%，检测对病人95%报阳，对健康人5%误报。取10万人：病人1000，其中950阳性；健康99000，误报4950。阳性共5900人，真患病950，概率约16%。这就是贝叶斯公式：P(病|阳)=P(阳|病)×P(病)/P(阳)，分子是真阳性数，分母是全部阳性数。关键区分：P(阳|病)是「病人报阳的把握」，P(病|阳)才是「阳性后患病的可能」，两者不是一回事。健康人基数太大，5%的误报也堆出大量假阳性，把16%稀释了。条件一变：患病率若升到30%，同样的检测下阳性可信度大增。所以拿到阳性先别慌，要看这种病本来有多常见。","d03":"正反馈指输出回头加强输入，让变化自己喂养自己。麦克风靠近音箱：声音进话筒，放大后播出，又被话筒拾到，一圈比一圈响，几秒内变成刺耳啸叫。放大的原因不是它有意志，而是回路每一环都把上一环的变化往同一方向再推一把，转完一圈增量还在，于是滚成指数式增长。负反馈相反：输出回头抵消输入，空调到温度就停，把系统摁在稳定点。要分清：正负说的是方向，好坏是评价。血糖调节是负反馈，通常有益；市场恐慌时「跌→抛售→更跌」的正反馈放大灾难，而复利滚雪球同样机制却常是好事。是否可取，取决于被放大的变化本身。它也不会无限放大，终会被某种限制刹住，比如功放失真或市场见底。","v08":"Little's law says: in steady state, the average number of items in a system (L) equals the arrival rate (λ) times the average time each spends there (W): L = λW. Example: a coffee shop gets 10 customers per minute and each spends 3 minutes ordering and waiting; on average, 30 people are inside. The law assumes only stability — arrivals must not exceed capacity — nothing about arrival patterns or service distributions. Why it holds: each arrival must wait out everyone already there, so longer waits or faster arrivals both inflate the count, and the bookkeeping balances exactly. Use it diagnostically: if queue length doubles while the arrival rate stays flat, waiting time must have doubled. Change the conditions: once throughput is capped, pushing arrivals higher doesn't add throughput at all — the line just grows without bound, and the law's stability assumption is what breaks.","v03":"自然选择改变的从来不是个体的身体，而是种群里基因的比例。想象一群甲虫，浅色居多，偶有深色突变体。树林被烟熏黑后，深色甲虫不易被鸟发现，活下来并留下更多后代；深色后代继承深色基因，几代后种群以深色为主。这里没有甲虫「想变深」或「努力适应」——每只出生时什么色就是什么色，鸟只是无差别吃掉显眼的。变异先随机产生，环境只是筛子，把恰好更适应的组合留下。所以关键区分：个体一生不发生进化式改变，被改变的是「哪些个体有机会繁殖」。条件一变结论就变：树皮若刷白，浅色重新占优，方向跟着环境走。长颈鹿脖子长不是因为祖先伸脖子够树叶，而是短脖个体留下后代少——把筛子讲成努力，是这类讲解最常见的错法。","v06":"A deadlock is when two or more processes each hold a resource and wait forever for the other's, so none can proceed. Picture two threads and two locks: thread A locks file 1, then asks for lock 2; thread B locks file 2, then asks for lock 1. A gets 1, B gets 2, and now each blocks on the lock the other holds. Nothing external failed — each is waiting for an event only its opponent can cause. Four conditions must hold simultaneously: mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Break any one and deadlock cannot form. The usual fix attacks circular wait: impose a global ordering so every thread takes lock 1 before lock 2 — B's first request then simply blocks until A finishes, which is waiting, not deadlock. Distributed systems show the same shape when transactions hold row locks while requesting each other's rows.","v05":"信息熵衡量结果揭晓前你有多没底，单位是比特：把每个结果的概率p代入−p·log₂p再加总。小概率的结果很「惊人」，但很少发生，乘起来贡献不大。公平硬币正反各半，你毫无偏向，熵为1比特；两面同花的硬币毫无悬念，熵为0；掰成9:1，十次能猜中九次，熵约0.47，介于其间。均匀最不确定的直觉是：只要某结果概率偏高，你就有了下注依据，悬念随之减少；所有选项势均力敌时，任何预测都最没把握。注意前提：「均匀最不确定」只在候选结果数固定时成立。若一个分布把概率摊到更多可能结果上，熵反而更大——所以掷骰子的熵高于掷硬币。此外现实很少完全均匀，估计出的熵总带一点误差。","v01":"过拟合就是「把做过的题背得太死，遇到新题就翻车」。机器学习是让程序从大量例子里找规律，比如给它一万张猫狗照片学分类。规律抠得太狠，连噪声都当成了规律——某张「猫」其实是靠角落里的沙发认出来的。结果训练里的照片全对，来一张没见过的照片就错。判断标准很明确：训练数据上成绩好、新数据上成绩差，是过拟合；两边都差是「根本没学会」，别混淆。为什么会这样？数据有限又带偶然细节，模型足够灵活时，总能找到一条既贴合规律又贴合噪声的规则。应对办法：给更多例子、限制模型复杂度（不许记沙发）、或留出一部分数据专门当「新题」检验。迁移一下：像学生刷题只对答案不总结，题型一变就不会——同一个机制。","d01":"似然回答：若某假设为真，看到手头这批数据的可能性有多大；后验回答：看到数据后，这假设有多可信。方向正好相反。掷硬币十次九正：固定这批数据，比较「公平(0.5)」与「偏(0.9)」两个假设，后者的似然高得多，所以数据支持「偏」。注意似然是相对的，只在几个假设之间比大小，单独的绝对值没什么意义。后验=似然×先验再归一：P(假设|数据)∝P(数据|假设)×P(假设)。先验是观察前的信任：若你本来就极信硬币公平，九正一反后可能仍偏信公平；先验不同，同一批数据推出不同后验。条件变化：数据越多，似然之间的差异被放大得越厉害，先验的影响随之变小——这是两者能统一的条件。","d07":"相关只说两个量同涨同跌，因果说动其中一个会改变另一个。例子：某城统计发现冰淇淋销量与溺水人数同起同落，相关很强。若是因果，禁售冰淇淋就该减少溺水，显然荒唐。真正的推手是第三者——夏天气温高，既让人买冰淇淋，也让人下河游泳，这叫混杂因素。看到相关先问三条路：A导致B、B导致A、还是C同时推动两者？人为干预是关键检验——只锁定A不动，看B变不变。把气温作为条件固定下来（只在32度的日子里比较），冰淇淋与溺水的相关基本消失，说明那层相关是气温带来的影子；若固定后依然存在，才值得怀疑有直接因果。所以完整说法是：相关不等于因果，除非你能排除混杂、并通过干预检验。","d02":"Variance answers: how spread out are the numbers around their average? The average alone hides this — {49, 50, 51} and {0, 50, 100} both average 50 but feel completely different. Population variance is the mean of squared distances from the mean: subtract the average from each number (its deviation), square it, then average the squares. For {49,50,51}: deviations −1, 0, 1, variance = 2/3. For {0,50,100}: variance = 2500. Squaring does more than remove minus signs — one miss of 50 weighs as much as 2500 misses of 1, so variance deliberately emphasizes big outliers; that emphasis, not the sign-fixing alone, is what makes squaring the chosen operation. Change one condition: double every number and the variance quadruples, since it scales with the square. That's why people often quote its square root, the standard deviation, which comes back in the original units.","d08":"Compound growth means the gain itself earns gains: each period grows the whole current balance, not just the original amount. At 10% a year, 100 becomes 110, and next year grows by 11, not 10 — the first year's interest now counts as principal. After n years the balance is start × (1.1)ⁿ. The multiplier is identical for everyone, so all differences come from the starting amount — that's exactly why it matters: growth is proportional, so a bigger base harvests bigger absolute gains at the same rate. Start with 1000 instead of 100 and after ten years you hold 2594 versus 259; the gap widens from 900 to 2335. The same math powers epidemics and nuclear chains, and it cuts both ways: credit-card debt at 20% doubles roughly every 3.6 years. The earlier a base exists, the more rounds of multiplication it experiences.","d06":"A cache is a fast copy of slow data kept nearby — say user profiles held in memory instead of the database. Reads get quick, but you've created a copy that can go stale: when the real data changes, the copy must be thrown out or refreshed. That's cache invalidation — deciding when a stored copy is no longer trustworthy. Example: a shop caches \"price: 100\" for a product, then cuts the real price to 80. Until the entry is invalidated, customers see 100; if they're charged it, the stale copy caused real harm. Common strategies: delete the entry whenever the underlying data changes, or attach a time-to-live so copies expire after, say, 60 seconds — trading freshness for fewer database hits. The hard part is the stale window itself: invalidate too eagerly and the cache buys you nothing; too lazily and users act on wrong data.","v04":"Idempotency means running the same operation any number of times has the same effect as running it once. Distributed systems care because networks are unreliable and clients retry: a payment request times out — did the server process it? Unknown. Retry and you might charge twice. An idempotent design makes retry safe. Contrast: \"set balance to 100\" is idempotent; \"add 10\" is not — two executions give +20. The standard fix is an idempotency key: attach a unique key to each logical operation, and the server, seeing a key it has already processed, returns the original result instead of executing again. Boundary to note: idempotency is about the observable effect, not byte-identical responses — a create-order API returning the same order either way is exactly what matters. Retries are inevitable; idempotency is what turns them from a correctness hazard into a harmless nuisance.","v02":"You search a document collection for \"invoices\" and get 20 results, of which 10 are truly invoices. Precision answers: of what I returned, how much is right? 10/20 = 50% — half the results are noise. Recall answers: of all invoices that exist (say 40 in the collection), how many did I find? 10/40 = 25%. They pull in opposite directions: loosen the filter to catch more invoices and junk slips in (recall up, precision down); tighten it and you miss real ones. Which matters more depends on which error costs more: spam filtering punishes false positives (real mail thrown away), so precision rules; cancer screening or legal discovery punishes false negatives, so recall rules. F1, the harmonic mean, summarizes when you need one number — it stays low if either side is low, unlike a plain average. And one number alone misleads: 100% precision with 1% recall just means you returned a single correct document.","d04":"Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you give up when you choose one thing. A free afternoon: you could nap, study for Friday's exam, or play basketball. You pick basketball. The cost isn't all the other options combined — just the single best one you sacrificed, say the study session; and if rest mattered most to you, then studying was the cost. This is why \"free\" rarely is: even a free concert costs the afternoon you could have spent otherwise. Money needn't change hands for a cost to exist — time spent one way cannot be spent another. Watch the boundary: sunk costs don't belong in the comparison. A ticket you already bought for an event you no longer want to attend is gone either way; compare only what each option gives you going forward.","v07":"公共物品有两个特征：非排他（没法把不付钱的人挡在门外）和非竞争（多一人享用不减少别人的份）。路灯、国防、防洪堤是典型——你无法只让交钱的人走亮灯的路。搭便车钻的正是「非排他」的空子：既然不交钱也照样享受，理性的选择就是不出钱，等别人埋单。后果是供给不足：一条街十户人家都想要路灯，每户出100元即可，但每户都盘算「我出不出灯都亮」，结果没人出，所有人都受损。这说明市场在此失灵——私人物品靠「付钱才给用」实现定价与供给，公共物品做不到。条件一变结论就变：开源软件靠声誉和捐赠补上激励，有些服务可用加密或收费墙恢复排他性。所以现实中公共物品常由税收供养，把搭便车变成强制分摊。"}
